test_title: SSC MTS 2024 Official Paper (Held On: 05 Nov, 2024 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: Which of the following Articles is automatically suspended when an emergency is declared on the grounds of external aggression?
solution:
The Correct answer is __**Article 19**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Article 19** of the Indian Constitution guarantees the fundamental rights to **freedom**, such as freedom of speech and expression, assembly, association, movement, residence, and profession.
 
• During a **National Emergency** declared on the grounds of **external aggression** or war, the rights guaranteed under Article 19 are automatically suspended to ensure **national security**.
 
• The suspension of Article 19 allows the government to impose **necessary restrictions** on freedoms to address the emergency effectively.
 
• This automatic suspension aligns with the need to balance **individual rights** with the **security and sovereignty** of the nation during critical situations.
 
• Article 19 is a part of the **Fundamental Rights** under Part III of the Indian Constitution, which are subject to certain restrictions during emergencies.
 
• The emergency provision is governed by **Article 352** of the Constitution, which provides the framework for declaring a National Emergency.
 
• Historically, Article 19 was suspended during significant emergencies such as the **Indo-China War (1962)**, the **Indo-Pakistan War (1971)**, and the **National Emergency (1975-77)**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• Unlike Article 19, Article 32 is not automatically suspended during emergencies; however, its application may be restricted in certain cases.
 
 
 
• Article 22**__
 __
 
• **Article 22** deals with protection against **arrest and detention** in certain cases.
 
• It provides safeguards such as the right to be informed of the grounds of arrest and the right to legal representation.
 
• During emergencies, preventive detention laws may override the protections under Article 22.
 
 
 
• **Article 35**__
 
 
• **Article 35** empowers the Parliament to make laws to enforce Fundamental Rights.
 
• It is not directly related to suspension during emergencies but plays a significant role in the legislative framework for Fundamental Rights.
